name: Youform
tagline: Affordable Typeform-style forms with logic, branding, and integrations

pricing.notes: Working normalization from the official public pricing structure. Recheck the source page immediately before publication.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: Unlimited forms, responses and questions; 1 user; 10 MB maximum file upload.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: Unlimited forms, responses and questions; 3 team members.

tiers.name: Business
tiers.limits: Unlimited forms, responses and questions; 5 included team members.

pricing.freeTierCaps: Unlimited forms, responses and questions; 1 user; 10 MB maximum file upload.
pricing.billingTerms: Monthly + annual; annual pricing is displayed as approximately 33% lower and is billed yearly.
pricing.hiddenCosts: Business seats above the included 5 cost $10/month each; phone OTP uses the customer's own Twilio account and therefore creates separate Twilio usage charges; uploads are subject to fair-use controls.

verdictSummary: Youform's solo core is compact: build a conversational forms tool with a schema-based form editor, public share link, validation, response table, CSV export, and webhook. A competent builder can reach a useful personal version in one sitting, while the paid product mainly wins on delivery, integrations, compliance.
coreLoopDIY: Build a conversational forms tool with a schema-based form editor, public share link, validation, response table, CSV export, and webhook.
replacementScope: personal replacement for the core loop
requirements: SMTP or transactional email key in .env
whatYouLose: spam and abuse defense at scale
whyPeopleStillPay: Youform: Customers pay for dependable collection, spam control, notifications, integrations, and confidence that responses will not disappear.
ongoingBurden: Own storage, webhooks, email delivery, spam, file uploads, privacy requests, schema changes, and uptime.

priorArt.name: HeyForm
priorArt.desc: Open-source form builder and collection backend.

alternatives.name: HeyForm
alternatives.desc: Typeform's manners, minus the monthly rent

facts.install: Hosted signup, or Docker Compose with MongoDB and KeyDB/Redis
facts.engines: Optional OpenAI-compatible API for AI features; default model documented as gpt-3.5-turbo-0125
facts.dataFormat: Hosted data lives in HeyForm Cloud; self-hosted forms and responses live in MongoDB, cache/session data in KeyDB/Redis, and uploads on the server or S3-compatible storage.
facts.gapVsPaid: HeyForm delivers the one-question-at-a-time experience, but self-hosting brings database and infrastructure work and its integration ecosystem is less turnkey than Youform's.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting needs Docker, a domain, reverse proxy/TLS, email configuration, and persistent database/storage volumes.

alternatives.name: Typebot
alternatives.desc: Conversational forms with deep branching; self-hosting is free under a fair-source licence

facts.install: Hosted signup, or Docker Compose/manual deployment of builder and viewer
facts.engines: Connects to OpenAI, Anthropic, Mistral, ElevenLabs and Dify through built-in integration blocks; API credentials are supplied by the user
facts.dataFormat: Hosted bots and results live in Typebot Cloud; self-hosted data lives in PostgreSQL and uploaded files in S3-compatible object storage.
facts.gapVsPaid: Typebot has exceptional branching and integrations, but its chatbot-style canvas and runtime are a different, more technical authoring model than Youform's conventional Typeform-style forms.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting requires PostgreSQL, S3-compatible storage, two web apps, DNS/TLS and mail/auth configuration; the licence is Fair Source rather than OSI open source.

alternatives.name: OpnForm
alternatives.desc: Open-source forms with unlimited respondents; the free self-hosted builder team stops at two

facts.install: Hosted signup, or the production Docker deployment
facts.dataFormat: Hosted data lives in OpnForm Cloud; self-hosted forms and submissions live in MySQL or PostgreSQL, with uploaded files on configured local or object storage.
facts.gapVsPaid: OpnForm is flexible and self-hostable, but the free self-hosted workspace stops at two users and the finished forms are less visually refined than Youform's.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting requires Docker, a database, a public domain/TLS and mail/storage configuration; the free self-hosted edition allows two workspace users.

alternatives.name: Tally
alternatives.desc: A generous hosted form builder; branding and custom domains are the upsell

facts.engines: Tally AI is available, but its underlying model provider is not publicly documented
facts.dataFormat: Forms and responses live in Tally's EU-hosted cloud; responses can be downloaded as CSV or synchronized to Google Sheets or Notion.
facts.gapVsPaid: Tally is a generous hosted substitute, but custom domains, branding removal, and some advanced presentation controls are paid rather than included.

rejectedAlternatives.name: TellForm
rejectedAlternatives.desc: A once-famous Typeform clone; archived since 2019, which is a long time to trust a form endpoint

notes: Strong page because Youform separates a compact personal workflow from the value of long-term polish.
prompt:
Build a usable personal replacement for the core loop of Youform.
Use exactly this stack: Next.js 15 + TypeScript + SQLite.
Primary job: Build a conversational forms tool with a schema-based form editor, public share link, validation, response table, CSV export, and webhook.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: spam and abuse defense at scale; large integration and template catalog; compliance controls and guaranteed delivery.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
